top_authentic_signals.name: Lighting Physics & Contrast Geometry
top_authentic_signals.summary: The image shows real camera clipping - 3.70% blown highlights and 0.05% crushed shadows - the physical trace of a sensor that ran out of dynamic range.
top_authentic_signals.what_found: 3.70% of pixels are burned to near-white and 0.05% are crushed to near-black. This is the hallmark of a real camera encountering more contrast than its sensor could handle, for example, a bright sky against a shaded subject. AI generators don't face physical saturation limits, so they almost never produce this kind of natural clipping.
top_authentic_signals.why_it_matters: Clipping is not a mistake - it's a physical inevitability when a real sensor meets a high-contrast scene. Because AI computes light mathematically, it rarely produces authentic-looking sensor clipping, making its presence here a meaningful signal for authenticity.
top_authentic_signals.caveat: HDR post-processing, tone mapping, strong flash, and professional retouching can all alter exposure profiles - introducing 'AI-like' qualities into real photos or vice versa.

top_ai_signals.name: Spectral Artifacts
top_ai_signals.summary: The Six-Lens model scored this image 92.6% AI / 7.4% authentic — a extremely high-confidence finding toward synthetic generation.
top_ai_signals.what_found: All six spectral lenses — visual texture (ConvNeXt), frequency grids (FFT), sensor noise simulation (SRM), color-space fingerprints (YCbCr), spatial reconstruction (SPAI), and robustness testing — collectively scored this image 92.6% AI. A score this strong, the majority of lenses independently flagged patterns like periodic frequency grids and noise distributions inconsistent with any known camera sensor profile.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: This model looks for patterns invisible to the human eye — buried in the pixel-level math of the image. A 92.6% score means the statistical fingerprint aligns significantly more with AI generation than camera physics, and these frequency-domain traces are very hard to remove without visibly degrading the image.
top_ai_signals.caveat: Heavy JPEG compression, aggressive resizing, or strong image filters can partially destroy the frequency-domain signals this model depends on, potentially softening a confident AI detection into an inconclusive result. Conversely, very new or unusual AI generators not present in training data may produce lower-than-expected scores.
